title: Where to Celebrate Diwali Across Victoria: Two Big Melbourne Festivals and Dandenong
excerpt: Diwali falls on November 8, but Victoria celebrates on October 31 — free festivals at Federation Square and Marvel Stadium Square, fireworks over the Yarra, and Dandenong on November 1.
body:
• Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026 in Australia — Victoria's big public celebrations are concentrated on Saturday, October 31.
  • Two free Melbourne festivals run the same day: the Victorian Festival of Diwali at Federation Square (11:30am-10pm, with fireworks) and Melbourne Diwali at Marvel Stadium Square, Docklands (2pm-10pm).
  • Dandenong follows on Sunday, November 1 from 4pm at Dandenong Park, 174 Lonsdale Street.
  • All three are free. For Docklands, Southern Cross Station is a five-minute walk and trams 70, 75 and 86 stop nearby — but October 31 is also Derby Day, so allow extra time.

Victoria's Diwali calendar this year is built around one crowded Saturday. Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, and the state's two largest public celebrations both take place a week earlier, on Saturday, October 31 — close enough together in central Melbourne that a determined family could do both. Here is what is on, where, and how to plan it, drawn from the organisers' own listings.

Federation Square: the Victorian Festival of Diwali

The Victorian Festival of Diwali returns to Federation Square for its 21st year, presented by Celebrate India Inc. with support from Fed Square. The programme runs from 11:30am to 10pm across the Main Square and Birrarung Marr Walk, according to the organiser's listing, with live music, classical, folk and Bollywood dance, kirtan, yoga and meditation workshops, and craft activities for children. A bazaar sells handcrafted goods and jewellery, food stalls line the riverside walk, and the evening closes with fireworks over the Yarra River. Participating Melbourne landmarks will be lit in pink and purple for the occasion.

"Come for the food, the music or the dance, but stay for the feeling of belonging. Everyone is welcome, and entry is free."

— Vani Bhatt (Pandya), Festival Coordinator, via The Australia Today

Federation Square sits opposite Flinders Street Station, so every metro line works. This year's festival supports Kids Helpline as its charity partner. Details are on the festival report in The Australia Today.

Docklands: Melbourne Diwali at Marvel Stadium Square

Five minutes from Southern Cross Station, Melbourne Diwali runs from 2pm to 10pm at Marvel Stadium Square, 740 Bourke Street, Docklands. It is managed by SarasCare, a not-for-profit community organisation, and entry is free with no ticket required. The main stage carries the Melbourne Diwali dance competition through the afternoon — about 40 dance groups from across Victoria — followed by the Diwali lighting ceremony at dusk and an evening showcase.

Around the stage there are more than 60 stalls, an all-vegetarian food market (chaat, dosa, mithai, lassi and masala chai), an artisan market selling diyas, jewellery, clothing, spices and gifts, a supervised Kids Zone, and hands-on stations for henna, rangoli and saree draping. The square is Melbourne's largest undercover event space, so the festival goes ahead rain or shine; it is step-free throughout and alcohol-free. The organisers' practical warning: October 31 is also Derby Day, so trains into the city will be full — come by train or tram (routes 70, 75 and 86, inside the Free Tram Zone) and allow extra time. The afternoon is the calmer time to visit with young children.

Beyond the CBD: Dandenong

For the south-east, the Diwali Festival in Dandenong runs on Sunday, November 1 from 4pm at Dandenong Park, 174 Lonsdale Street, Dandenong. The listing promises live cultural performances, Bollywood music, traditional dance, Indian food stalls, shopping booths and kids' activities — a neighbourhood-scale alternative to the two city festivals, and the closest major event for the large Indian community in Melbourne's south-east.

Planning your Diwali week

The workable plan for most families: pick one of the two October 31 festivals as your main event — Federation Square for the fireworks finale, Marvel Stadium Square for the dance competition and the undercover guarantee — use the artisan markets to buy diyas and mithai for home, and keep Sunday, November 8 itself for puja and family. If you are in the south-east, Dandenong on November 1 splits the difference. All of the events above are free; check the organisers' pages before travelling, as programmes can change closer to the day.
